why: Quote verified verbatim at line 36 of the fetched page (curl, not WebFetch); the whole line is that one sentence and the block's second paragraph is a separate 'Also this week' line, so nothing reverses it. The cited file is accurate too: apps/cli/src/index.ts:2120-2245 dispatches help/version/run/validate/doctor/plugin/ping/health/versions/workspaces/sessions/connections/sources/session/send/cancel/invoke/listen and has no 'mcp' branch. But the finding's CONSEQUENCE is false, which is the exact 'identifier unwired, consequence handled one layer up' shape this repo's audit history warns about. The headless server the CLI talks to registers the OAuth handlers (packages/server/src/index.ts:265 -> registerCoreRpcHandlers -> registerOAuthHandlers in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/index.ts), and those channels take an MCP-server target directly: oauth:start accepts pluginServer {pluginKey, serverName} (oauth.ts:467-495) and oauth:revoke accepts the same (oauth.ts:728-747), calling deletePluginMcpServerCredentials, which deletes both the oauth and bearer credential rows (packages/shared/src/plugins/mcp-credentials.ts:71-83). Neither needs an interactive surface: assertPendingAuthRequestBinding returns early when sessionId and authRequestId are both absent (oauth.ts:776-778), so there is no session or pending auth-request prerequisite. The CLI reaches them through its documented raw-RPC verb, 'invoke <channel> [json-args...]' (apps/cli/src/index.ts:915-935, listed in printHelp), which applies no channel allowlist. So `nessy-general-agent invoke oauth:revoke '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` is a complete, non-interactive, shell-only equivalent of `claude mcp logout`, and `invoke oauth:start '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` starts the login flow from the shell and returns {authUrl,state,flowId}; only the authorization-code capture is manual, because oauth:complete takes {flowId, code, state} (oauth.ts:580-584) and the local callback listener is run by the desktop/electron client rather than by the CLI. Two secondary points. (1) The stated evidence 'grep -ra -F "mcp login" over packages/ apps/ -> 0 hits' is itself wrong: hits exist in apps/electron/dist/resources/bin/codex/darwin-x64/codex-app-server, but they are Codex's own `codex mcp login` strings, i.e. a sibling subsystem, so they do not support the finding either. (2) The absence of a named CLI mcp namespace is a product-shape difference already on record, not an unnoticed gap: this fork's CLI is a thin websocket client to the desktop/headless server and carries no mcp verbs at all (no add/list/remove either), and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-3.md:291 already records 'documented, impossible on Nessy - no `claude mcp list` equivalent' for exactly this surface, with docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-plugin-install-usability.md:341 recording the related per-server-vs-one-system-login deviation for dp-backed servers. It is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.
correctedState: The CLI has no named `mcp` subcommand, so there is no `mcp login`/`mcp logout` verb - but a shell path to authenticate and de-authenticate an MCP server does exist, so the finding's second clause is wrong. The headless server serves oauth:start / oauth:complete / oauth:revoke with a `pluginServer {pluginKey, serverName}` target and no session or pending-auth-request prerequisite, and the CLI's documented `invoke <channel> [json]` verb reaches them with no allowlist. `nessy-general-agent invoke oauth:revoke '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` is a full headless equivalent of `claude mcp logout` (it deletes both the oauth and bearer credential rows), and `invoke oauth:start '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` starts the flow from the shell; only the authorization-code capture must be done by hand before `invoke oauth:complete`, because the local callback listener lives in the desktop client, not the CLI. The residual divergence is ergonomic - no named verb and no CLI-side callback listener - not 'MCP OAuth is reachable only through the app's interactive surfaces'. It also sits inside an already-recorded product-shape deviation: the fork's CLI carries no mcp namespace at all, and deviation-unit-3.md:291 records 'no `claude mcp list` equivalent' for the same surface.
